description:
Israeli settler violence and land confiscation in the occupied West Bank have reached record levels. In an interview with Al Jazeera, historian Zachary Foster said this is "the most right-wing government in all of Israeli history", with right-wing parties competing to be "the most violent and the most genocidal towards Palestinians". He said "the Nakba never ended", arguing that Israel has been on a "58-year project of expelling Palestinians" since 1967 through policies that strip Palestinians of residency and physical displacement. Foster said change will not come from within Jewish-Israeli society, citing polls which he said showed significant support for the expulsion and killing of Palestinians. He argued that pressure must come from outside through sanctions, boycotts, divestment, protests and direct action, pointing to Palestine Action's campaign against arms factories supplying Israel.

author: Al Jazeera English
description: Following the US preemptive strike on Iran's Larak Island and Iran's missile retaliation against US bases in Jordan, Sina Azodi, director of the Middle East Studies Program at George Washington University, told Al Jazeera that it is "really up to the American side" whether the conflict escalates further. He warned that if the US responds, Iran will be "left with no choice" but to respond, potentially leading back to "full military confrontation." Azodi said the US claim that Iran was preparing to launch sea mines from Larak is "quite possible", given Tehran's desire to assert control over the Strait of Hormuz. He said both sides are engaged in a "war of narratives" over the strait, with President Trump's claims about keeping it open also aimed at calming energy markets ahead of the US midterm elections. Azodi said Iran's targeting of Jordan was deliberate, given its strained relations with Amman, and intended to signal that "any American base in the region can be a potential target."
title: Why did Iran target US bases in Jordan? Sina Azodi explains

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
The US has struck Iran's Larak Island in a preemptive attack to prevent the IRGC from laying sea mines in the Strait of Hormuz, prompting Iranian missile strikes on US bases in Jordan. 
In an interview with Al Jazeera, former Pentagon Director of Arabian Peninsula Affairs David Des Roches said the specificity of the US operation suggests Washington is "actually doing what it says it is" by targeting missiles capable of laying mines. 
He said Iran's response will be "interesting to see" and noted the US is showing "unusual restraint", possibly due to the election runoff. 
Des Roches said Iran has "never been in full control" of the Strait but has a "disruptive capability" that can be exerted with a fraction of the effort needed to ensure control. 
He warned that "the longer they keep the Straits impeded, the less important it becomes", noting East Asian countries are already shifting their energy strategy away from the Gulf towards the US.

title: US struck Larak Island to prevent Iran mining Strait of Hormuz: Analysis

author: Al Jazeera English
description:
Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) has launched strikes on two US airbases in Jordan — King Hussein and al-Azraq — using ballistic missiles. 
Jordan's armed forces say they intercepted eight missiles in Jordanian airspace. 
The IRGC says the attack was in response to US strikes on Iran's Larak Island. 
A senior US official confirmed that US forces bombed two IRGC rocket launchers on Larak Island, marking the first known US attack on Iran in a month. 
Washington says the strike was preemptive, aimed at preventing the IRGC from placing mines in the Strait of Hormuz. 
CENTCOM rejected Iran's claim that the US strike was an act of aggression, calling it "absolutely false". 
The IRGC says several soldiers and civilians were killed in the US strikes. 
The exchange marks the most significant US-Iran military escalation in weeks, after the Trump administration had shifted towards economic pressure. 

Al Jazeera's Manuel Rapalo reports from Washington, DC, and Sinem Koseoglu from
title: Iran strikes US bases in Jordan after US attacks IRGC targets on Larak Island
